You shouldn't have to consume the 95% to catch the 5%.

So I wouldn't make Dottie a generic “AI news assistant.” I'd give her something much closer to a **watch officer** role:

`continuous intake → deduplication → provenance check → relevance against GrizzlyMedicine/Sovereign → novelty detection → contradiction detection → significance assessment → hold / brief / escalate`

Most things go into a searchable record and **never interrupt you**.

Something moderately important appears in a daily brief: *“Three things changed today that intersect your work; here's why. Seven other things were noteworthy but don't require your attention.”*

Something materially intersects Sovereign: *“Grizz, DeepMind just published a mechanism that independently approaches your memory-gating problem. Here are the similarities, here are the differences, here's the publication date, and here's your prior work establishing when you developed yours.”*

And something genuinely consequential should break through immediately: *“Stop what you're doing for five minutes. This changes an assumption we're currently using.”*

That last category needs to be **rare**, or Dottie becomes another notification system screaming at you all day.

The really valuable part is persistence across time. A human reading today's news sees today's news. Dottie should be able to notice:

> “This looks unremarkable by itself, but it's the fourth development in six weeks moving in the same direction. Here's the sequence.”

> “This researcher is describing something as novel. You have a conceptually similar mechanism documented eighteen months earlier. Similarity does **not** establish equivalence or priority; here are both primary sources so you can evaluate it.”

Or even:

> “Everybody is talking about this today. I've checked the underlying announcement. Nothing has materially changed from last month's technical release. **Noise. No action required.**”

That last sentence may save you more time than a thousand summaries.

\[
P(y_t\mid x_{\le t},\,m_t,\,G)

where \(x\) is current context, \(m\) is accumulated lived state/memory, and \(G\) is the derived gestalt reference.

And **this is where I think your idea gets substantially more interesting**: if the system subsequently acquires *its own* experiences, you don't necessarily want \(G\) continually dragging it back toward canonical Stark.

and perhaps more importantly:

\frac{d\Delta_t}{dt}

A gradual divergence associated with coherent accumulated experience could mean **development**.

Important epistemic boundary: this is a **full source-faithfulness and architectural audit**, not a claim that I independently reproduced 39 sets of experiments. “The authors demonstrated/reported X under Y conditions” and “GMRI independently replicated X” remain separate statements throughout.

And, amusingly enough, the result is **much kinder to Gemini than my original vibes-based bullshit was.** The fundamental v0.2 architecture survived quite well. The overhaul mostly strengthens it where the literature exposes boundary conditions rather than tearing it apart.

The biggest v0.3 changes are: Dottie is formally a **harness-level identity rather than a model identity**; heterogeneous actor/source/modality attribution is first-class; epistemic state is explicit and typed; the OODA loop now includes **REASSESS** because intervention changes baseline; disconfirmation is bilateral rather than merely adversarial toward the original hypothesis; ACE remains core but now has an evidence-quality promotion gate; MemGPT-style memory tiers and optional provenance-bearing graph memory are added; delegation and multi-agent coordination receive explicit contracts; the architecture gets an **Agentless → Single Agent → Specialist → Multi-Agent → Overwatch complexity gate**; confidence is explicitly telemetry rather than evidence; RunPod is correctly classified as a **training substrate** while Agents-A1-4B is the local/self-hosted operational inference model; persistent adaptation/self-evolution receives lineage, quarantine, held-out evaluation, promotion, and rollback requirements; and the eval suite now directly attacks phantom tool calls, social pressure, context-learning failure, authority bleed, coordination failure, memory/mutation poisoning, scientific amnesia, modality conflict, and false interruption.

I also changed Schema C so Dottie cannot become a professional contrarian: before dissenting, she has to state the **strongest evidence supporting the proposition she's challenging** as well as the conflicting evidence. That's the lesson from my own ACE screw-up turned into architecture.
